item.title: Upper-Limb MLD Principles After Breast-Cancer Treatment
clinicalUse: Selected upper-limb lymphedema after appropriate medical assessment
patientPosition: Supine or supported sitting with arm elevated comfortably and skin accessible.
contact: Flat broad hands using very light skin-stretch contact.
forceDirection: Follow the drainage sequence appropriate to intact lymphatic pathways as taught in formal lymphedema training.
dosage: Session length is individualized within complete decongestive therapy; manual work is not used alone.
steps: 1. Exclude cellulitis, DVT and acute cardiac decompensation.
3. Use proximal/central preparation according to training.
6. Combine with compression, exercise and skin care.
mistakes: Using MLD without compression/exercise when indicated.
safety: Do not perform during acute cellulitis, untreated DVT or acute decompensated heart failure.
item.visualCue: Very light skin stretch → trained drainage sequence → compression + exercise + skin care.

subTechniques.name: Proximal Preparation
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Prepare proximal pathways before distal limb work
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, side-lying or sitting with the arm supported.
subTechniques.contact: Region-specific contact over Trunk/axillary drainage territories using the parent technique principles.
subTechniques.direction: Very light rhythmic skin stretch following trained lymphatic sequence
subTechniques.dosage: Use a conservative response-guided trial and reassess before repeating.
subTechniques.reassess: Heaviness, skin feel and limb measurement

subTechniques.name: Upper-Limb Sequence
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Support fluid movement within a complete decongestive plan
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, side-lying or sitting with the arm supported.
subTechniques.contact: Region-specific contact over Arm/forearm/hand using the parent technique principles.
subTechniques.direction: Proximal-to-distal preparation then distal-to-proximal working sequence as formally trained
subTechniques.dosage: Use a conservative response-guided trial and reassess before repeating.
